name: Use of Hard-coded Password
description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: The gallery routes expose DeleteImage and DeleteAll with only HttpPost; there is no controller/action authorization, ownership check, global Authorize filter, or web.config authorization restriction. Any reachable anonymous caller can invoke DeleteAll to delete every block blob using the application storage identity (158-162), or DeleteImage to delete a known blob. This confers destructive storage modification permissions to arbitrary site visitors, not merely the intentionally public read access configured at line 66. Exploitation requires a configured storage account and initialized container; lack of anti-forgery checks also permits cross-site form submission.

name: Insufficient Logging
description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: Security-critical blob deletion (DeleteImage at 136 and DeleteAll at 162) is followed only by a redirect. No application audit record contains actor, target, outcome, or deletion count. Failure handlers (140-144, 168-172) send the exception to a view instead of recording it. Repository-wide application C# inspection found no audit/logging provider or logging calls; no storage diagnostic configuration is committed. Anonymous bulk deletion can therefore occur without an application-level security event record. External platform/storage logging may exist but cannot be verified from this repository.

name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
